subject: general
question: The Indian government has allocated ₹_____ for the National Film Development Corporation in the 2024-25 budget.
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹23 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian government has allocated ₹23 crore for the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) in the 2024-25 budget.
 
• NFDC is responsible for promoting and developing the Indian film industry.
 
• The allocation is aimed at supporting various initiatives to improve the quality and reach of Indian cinema.
 
• NFDC plays a crucial role in funding and facilitating the production and distribution of films that reflect Indian culture and heritage.
 
• This budget allocation will also help in the promotion of regional and independent cinema in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Film Development Corporation (NFDC)**

 
 
• Established in 1975, NFDC is a central agency under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India.
 
• Its primary objective is to promote high-quality Indian cinema, both domestically and internationally.
 
• NFDC provides financial assistance to filmmakers for the production of feature films, documentaries, and short films.
 
• It also organizes film festivals and markets to showcase Indian films globally.
 
• NFDC has been instrumental in the production of numerous critically acclaimed films that have garnered international recognition.
 
 
 
• **Indian Film Industry**
 
 
• The Indian film industry is one of the largest in the world, producing over 1,800 films annually.
 
• Bollywood, based in Mumbai, is the most significant segment, but regional cinema also plays a vital role in the industry.
 
• Indian films are known for their diverse genres, including drama, romance, action, and musicals.
 
• Indian cinema has a substantial following not only in India but also among the Indian diaspora worldwide.
 
• The industry contributes significantly to the Indian economy and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Budget Allocation for Arts and Culture**
 
 
• The Indian government allocates funds annually to support various arts and cultural initiatives.
 
• This includes funding for institutions like NFDC, the National School of Drama, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• The allocation aims to preserve and promote India's rich cultural heritage.
 
• It also supports training programs, cultural exchanges, and the production of cultural content.
 
• These initiatives help in nurturing talent and enhancing the global presence of Indian arts and culture.
